title: Project & Export
description: Manage projects on the Dashboard, configure Project Settings and auto-save, and export your game to Web (.ZIP), Windows (.EXE), or .lupisproject archives.

blocks.content: Lupis Engine stores your active projects in fast local storage and lets you package them into portable project archives, standalone HTML5 web builds, or Windows desktop executables.

items.title: Project Archives
items.desc: Save or load single-file **.lupisproject** bundles to back up or share your work.

items.title: Auto-Save & Snapshots
items.desc: Sync changes automatically on a timer and capture viewport cover thumbnails.

items.title: Web Standalone (.ZIP)
items.desc: Bundle your game into an HTML5 package ready for itch.io or any static web host.

items.title: Desktop App (.EXE)
items.desc: Compile your project into a standalone Windows executable for offline play.

blocks.content: You create, import, rename, and back up projects from the **My Projects** dashboard.

items: To import an existing project backup, drag and drop a **.lupisproject** file anywhere onto the **My Projects** dashboard, or click **Load Project** and select the file.
Right-click any project card on the dashboard to open its context menu.
Choose **Open** or **Open in New Tab** to launch the project in the [Editor Overview](interface/editor_overview) workspace.
Choose **Save Project** to download a compressed **.lupisproject** backup file to your computer.
Choose **Rename** or **Edit Description** to update the project's title and summary, or choose **Delete Project** to remove it from storage.

blocks.message: Clicking **Delete Project** permanently removes the project folder from storage and cannot be undone. Always export a **.lupisproject** archive first if you may need the project later.

blocks.content: Inside the editor, open **Project Settings** to configure your game's metadata, startup scene, canvas resolution, physics defaults, and storage synchronization.

rows: Manages project identity, cover images (**Upload Thumbnail** or **Capture Scene Now**), and storage sync.
Customizes theme and visual workspace behavior.
Sets the startup scene, frame rate (default **60 FPS**), UI layer bounds, and resolution presets.
Global gravity, drag coefficients, and world boundary limits
Configures default simulation forces applied to [Physics Body](components/physics_body) entities.
Grid snapping guidelines and default camera perspective
Controls alignment guides in the [Scene Viewport](interface/scene_viewport).
Collider wireframes and runtime performance overlays
Displays visual diagnostics while testing your game.
Packages your project into distributable builds or backup archives.

blocks.message: In **Project Info**, turn on **Enable Auto Save** and set **Auto Save Interval** (in minutes) so the editor writes unsaved modifications to storage automatically. You can also click **Revert Changes** before saving to reload the last saved state.

blocks.content: The **Publish & Export** tab (**Build & Publish Module**) in **Project Settings** provides three export formats.

rows: An HTML5 bundle containing the engine runtime, scripts, and assets, ready to upload to itch.io or any web server.
A standalone Windows executable package for offline desktop play.
A single compressed **.lupisproject** file containing all scenes, node graphs, and assets for backup or re-importing.

items: Press **Ctrl + S** (or click **Save Project** in **Project Settings**) so all recent scene and script edits are committed.
Open **Project Settings**, select **Engine & Canvas**, and confirm that **Initial Scene** and **Target Resolution** are set to your desired startup level and screen size.
Select the **Publish & Export** tab on the left sidebar of **Project Settings**.
For a web build, click **Export Web (.ZIP)**. Your browser downloads the packaged HTML5 **.zip** archive.
For a Windows build, click **Build App (.EXE)**, wait for the compilation to finish, and click the green **Download (.EXE)** button.

blocks.message: Compiling a **Desktop App (.EXE)** requires the backend service running on port **4000** (see [Installation & Setup](getting_started/installation#run-with-docker)).

rows: You need to start the Docker or Node.js backend service for **.EXE** desktop builds.
